title: Large Pretraining Datasets Don't Guarantee Robustness after Fine-Tuning in Image Classification
abstract: arXiv:2410.21582v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large-scale pretrained models are widely leveraged as foundations for learning new specialized tasks via fine-tuning, with the goal of maintaining the general performance of the model while allowing it to gain new skills. A valuable goal for all such models is robustness: the ability to perform well on out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks. We assess whether fine-tuning preserves the overall robustness of the pretrained model in image classification, and observed that models pretrained on large datasets exhibited strong catastrophic forgetting and loss of OOD generalization. To systematically assess robustness preservation in fine-tuned models, we propose the Robustness Inheritance Benchmark (ImageNet-RIB). The benchmark, which can be applied to any pretrained model, consists of a set of related but distinct OOD (downstream) tasks and involves fine-tuning on one of the OOD tasks in the set then testing on the rest. tldr: 该论文提出鲁棒性继承基准ImageNet-RIB，揭示了一个关键问题：即使在大规模数据集上预训练的模型，经微调后仍会出现严重的灾难性遗忘和分布外泛化能力丧失，因此大规模预训练并不保证微调后的鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Robustness Inheritance Benchmark (ImageNet-RIB) and reveals that large-scale pretraining does not guarantee robustness after fine-tuning, as fine-tuned models suffer severe catastrophic forgetting and loss of out-of-distribution generalization.
